takeaway: Long thoracic nerve injury paralyses serratus anterior: the scapula wings and the arm cannot be raised above the horizontal.

question.text: After a stab wound to the side of the right chest, a young man cannot raise his right arm above horizontal and his scapula protrudes. Which nerve is damaged?

lines.text: A stab wound on the side of the chest, and an odd problem with the shoulder.
The long thoracic nerve runs superficially over the serratus anterior muscle.
That makes it vulnerable, especially when the arm is raised. It supplies the serratus anterior.
Without it, the scapula moves laterally and backwards. This is a winged scapula.
And the serratus cannot rotate the glenoid upwards, so the arm will not go above the horizontal.
So the nerve damaged is the long thoracic nerve.
lines.say: (sigh) So the nerve damaged is the long thoracic nerve.
